title: Algorithmic fairness and bias mitigation for clinical machine learning with deep reinforcement learning
abstract: As models based on machine learning continue to be developed for healthcare applications, greater effort is needed to ensure that these technologies do not reflect or exacerbate any unwanted or discriminatory biases that may be present in the data. Here we introduce a reinforcement learning framework capable of mitigating biases that may have been acquired during data collection. In particular, we evaluated our model for the task of rapidly predicting COVID-19 for patients presenting to hospital emergency departments and aimed to mitigate any site (hospital)-specific and ethnicity-based biases present in the data. Using a specialized reward function and training procedure, we show that our method achieves clinically effective screening performances, while significantly improving outcome fairness compared with current benchmarks and state-of-the-art machine learning methods. We performed external validation across three independent hospitals, and additionally tested our method on a patient intensive care unit discharge status task, demonstrating model generalizability.

claims.text: The proposed reinforcement learning framework with specialized reward function achieves equalized odds for ethnicity debiasing in COVID-19 screening across external hospital cohorts.
In COVID-19 status prediction with ethnicity debiasing, the RL model achieved AUROC scores of 0.834 on PUH, 0.849 on UHB, and 0.923 on BH test sets.
For ICU patient discharge status prediction with ethnicity debiasing, the RL model achieved equalized odds standard deviations of 0.032 for true positives and 0.022 for false positives.

For mitigating hospital-site bias in COVID-19 status prediction, the weighted RL model achieved equalized odds standard deviations of 0.010 for true positives and 0.040 for false positives on a held-out multi-site test set.
The difference in accuracy between the RL model and comparator models across classification tasks was statistically significant (P < 0.0001 by Wilcoxon signed rank test).

A duelling double-deep Q-network framing classification with rewards inversely proportional to sensitive feature frequencies mitigates algorithmic bias without standard cross-entropy loss gradient descent.

limitations.text: The RL models did not completely fulfill equalized odds requirements, partly because the training datasets were imbalanced with respect to sensitive attributes.
Optimizing thresholds for high sensitivity (0.9) resulted in lower specificity for the RL models compared to some standard supervised baseline models.
Machine learning models trained on real-world clinical data often fail to generalize to new hospital settings due to site-specific measurement and collection biases.

future_work.text: Train future reinforcement learning debiasing models on demographically balanced datasets when sufficient data volume is available.
Explore site-specific decision thresholds tailored during calibration at each hospital deployment site to standardize predictive performance across settings.
Investigate model transferability to entirely new domains and assess potential residual bias transfer when deploying to different population distributions.

methodologies.name: Duelling Double-Deep Q-Network (DDQN) Bias Mitigation Framework
methodologies.description: A deep reinforcement learning framework using duelling Q-network architecture and a non-differentiable reward function inversely weighted by sensitive attribute frequency to train fair classifiers.
datasets: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (OUH)
